beats.title: Arrivals in Karawa
beats.boundaryReason: The session opens with separate arrival vignettes for the four characters and closes this introductory movement just before they converge on the disturbance in town.
dateEvidence: The manifest starts the session on 1748-03-21.
The opening narration places Kenzo's approach to Karawa in the morning light.

beats.title: The Hyenas Charge
beats.boundaryReason: The four characters converge, size one another up amid the emergency, and enter combat; the beat ends after Kenzo's opening flurry before the hyena's counterattack.
dateEvidence: This beat continues directly from the morning arrival scenes.
The DM explicitly confirms that the fight occurs in the morning.

beats.title: Hyenas Brought Down
beats.boundaryReason: The hyenas answer the party's first attacks and the remaining combat plays through to Wellby's killing strike on the final beast.
dateEvidence: This is the uninterrupted second phase of the same morning combat.
The beat ends with the final hyena expiring.

beats.title: Aftermath and Introductions
beats.boundaryReason: With the hyenas dead, the villagers scatter for help while the strangers tend the wounded, inspect the bodies, and begin introducing themselves.
dateEvidence: The beat begins immediately after the morning fight ends.
No travel or elapsed-time transition occurs before the party's conversation.

beats.title: Strangers Find Common Ground
beats.boundaryReason: The four strangers trade names and histories, compare what brought them to Karawa, and discover Delwath's concern about a disturbance in the Weave before help arrives.
dateEvidence: This conversation continues at the teahouse directly after the battle.
The transcript later still identifies the current time as morning.

beats.title: Karawa Asks for Help
beats.boundaryReason: Beli, Kisa, and Candrosa arrive to heal the wounded and assess the attack; Kisa asks Delwath to investigate after Beli's magic fails and the leaders depart.
dateEvidence: The leaders arrive during the same uninterrupted morning aftermath.
The beat ends when Kisa leaves to tend the villagers.

beats.title: The Investigation Begins
beats.boundaryReason: Delwath recruits the other three, the new group rests and equips itself, and Seeker visits the temple before everyone regathers to follow the beasts' tracks.
dateEvidence: Delwath explicitly says it is still morning as the group discusses the attack.
Only a short rest and preparation interval passes before departure.

beats.title: Tracks into the Badlands
beats.boundaryReason: The party leaves Karawa, follows the attackers northeast into the canyonlands, loses the trail, and climbs to a vantage where a distant dust cloud offers a new lead.
dateEvidence: The party departs after the same morning's attack and several hours of tracking pass.
The DM explicitly places the party in the early afternoon sun near the end of the beat.

beats.title: Alesh on the Old Road
beats.boundaryReason: The party intercepts Alesh, learns about Gomat and the dangers near Nashtkar, and decides to push toward the oasis after she rides on to Karawa.
dateEvidence: The party reaches Alesh an hour or two after the early-afternoon sighting.
The DM explicitly says it is about four in the afternoon during the travel discussion.

beats.title: Nightfall at Gomat
beats.boundaryReason: The party follows the old road, camps overnight, then pushes through the following day to reach Gomat after dark, where giant lizards feed among the silent tents.
dateEvidence: The party sets out after the four-in-the-afternoon conversation on 1748-03-21.
The transcript explicitly narrates a cold night, a long rest, and a pre-dawn departure on the following day.
The arrival in moonlight is therefore inferred to occur on 1748-03-22.
